PullRequest.Title: ci: run only the unit tests a change can affect on macOS and Windows
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## What


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/354ed24f-ebe3-44bf-a60f-32bc0fcbbe0a



Every pull request push runs every unit test on all three platforms. The macOS and Windows unit test jobs (`macOS / Electron-Unit`, `Windows / Electron-Unit`, `macOS (unit) / Browser`, `Windows (unit) / Browser`) take about 54 VM minutes per push, mostly on the billed macOS xlarge runners and the Windows pool, while a typical change can only affect a few percent of the unit tests.

This PR runs only the unit test files a change can affect on macOS and Windows. **Linux keeps running every unit test on every push.**

- **`build/ripple`** is a new Rust tool built on [oxc](https://oxc.rs). It reads both commits straight from git and analyzes every TypeScript module into runtime declarations with content hashes that ignore comments, formatting and type-only syntax. It links them into one graph (about 160k nodes) and lists the test files that depend on a changed declaration. A plan takes about a second. See [build/ripple/README.md](build/ripple/README.md).
- **`build/ripple/vscode.jsonc`** holds everything ripple knows about this repository (see below). The Rust code only knows TypeScript, JavaScript, npm and git.
- **The existing `Detect Changes` job** now also runs `ripple plan` on the merge commit, uploads the selected unit test files as the `unit-test-plan` artifact and writes a summary to the job page, so no extra VM is needed. It now uses a depth-2 checkout instead of a sparse one, and the planning steps never fail the job, so they cannot affect the change detection outputs. When ripple fails to build, pass its tests or plan, a new `Ripple` check fails for pull requests that change `build/ripple`. It reads the result of `Detect Changes` instead of repeating its work, and is skipped for other pull requests, which only get a warning (also when a module that ripple cannot parse disables selection). To block merges, `Ripple` needs to be added to the required checks of `main`; a skipped check passes. The binary is cached by its sources; the new `pr-ripple.yml` builds it on `main` when ripple changes, and checks daily that the cache still exists.
- **The macOS and Windows unit test jobs** download the plan and pass the list to the Electron, node.js and browser runners with a new `--runList <file>` option. Each runner runs the tests it would run by default, but only from the listed files, so ripple needs no knowledge of the runners. The steps are skipped when nothing is selected, and the browser runner exits without launching a browser when none of the listed files are browser tests.
- **Fallbacks:** the jobs run every unit test when planning fails, when the artifact cannot be downloaded, when the change touches a file every unit test depends on (`runEverything` in `vscode.jsonc`: the test runners and launchers, the transpiler, compiler options, runtime versions, the unit test jobs, and ripple itself), or when it affects more than half of the unit test work.
- Required check names don't change.
- Hygiene skips `*.toml` and `Cargo.lock` for the copyright and indentation checks.

## Repository configuration

Nothing about this repository is hard-coded in ripple. [`build/ripple/vscode.jsonc`](build/ripple/vscode.jsonc) lists, with comments:

- `modules` and `tests`: which files are analyzed, which are unit and integration tests, and which scripts run the unit tests (`runners`: the modules they load into every run, such as `assertCleanState`'s, count as dependencies of every test).
- `pathAliases`: `vs/` is `src/vs/`.
- `runEverything`: the files every unit test depends on, by the reason shown in the plan. ripple adds the scripts that the listed scripts load through relative imports, such as `build/lib/electronVersion.ts`.
- `packages`: npm packages that build or run every test but that no `runEverything` script loads (none today: ripple finds the packages those scripts load, such as mocha and the test runners' web server, itself), the npm scripts the unit test jobs run, and `package.json` fields no test reads (`distro`).
- `injectedGlobals`: `_VSCODE_PACKAGE_JSON` and `_VSCODE_PRODUCT_JSON`, so a `product.json` or `package.json` change selects the code that reads them.
- `pure` and `implicitMethods`: repository conventions that make the analysis more precise (`localize`, `URI`, `dispose`, ...).
- `moduleLoaders`: functions that load the package their first argument names (`importAMDNodeModule`).

Test data folders need no configuration: a folder next to test files that contains no module (`__snapshots__`, `fixtures`, `test-cases`) is read by the tests whose code, or a module they load, names it in a string. Neither do golden files read through a computed path: a template literal such as `` `vs/workbench/services/keybinding/test/node/${file}` `` reads the data files of that folder that match its static start and end.

Unknown fields are errors. Adding, say, a new launcher that every test depends on is a one-line change there.

## Why Linux still runs every unit test

- Static selection cannot see tests that depend on state another test file leaked into the same process. Those were the only misses in the recall check below, and the full Linux run still catches them before merge.
- The full Linux run keeps a complete baseline on every push. Nothing compares it with the plan automatically yet: a warning in the Linux unit test jobs when a failed test file is missing from the plan would measure recall continuously before selecting on Linux too.
- macOS and Windows are about 70% of the unit test minutes, and they are the expensive runners.

## Expected impact

Replaying the 2,184 pull request pushes of Oct 13-19: macOS and Windows would run 13.5% of their unit test work on average. 7% of pushes fall back to the full suite and 17% run no unit tests at all.

| Job | Today (mean) | With this PR (estimate) |
|---|---|---|
| macOS / Electron-Unit | 14.5 min | 3.4 min |
| Windows / Electron-Unit | 20.0 min | 5.3 min |
| macOS (unit) / Browser | 8.7 min | 3.1 min |
| Windows (unit) / Browser | 10.5 min | 4.0 min |

That is about 38 VM minutes less per push, about 13% of all pull request minutes, or about 14,000 VM minutes on a busy weekday.

## Validation

- **Recall on real failures:** 75 PR runs with failing Linux unit test jobs (Oct 17-20). ripple selected 34 of the 36 failures the PRs caused. The 2 misses were tests that only passed because other test files had leaked registrations into a global registry; Linux keeps catching these. Every macOS/Windows-only unit test failure caused by a PR in that period was in a selected test.
- **Replay of 708 merged PRs** (Oct 13-20): ripple selects 9.0% of the unit test work on average (median 1.9%); file-level import analysis would select 21.3%.
- **Moving the repository knowledge into `vscode.jsonc` changed no selection:** on the same 630 commits, the binaries before and after select the same unit test files, make the same run-everything decisions and count the same changed declarations and packages. The plans of 8 sampled commits are byte-identical, and the old hard-coded file rules and the configuration agree on all 20,946 repository paths. The only intended difference is that changes to `build/ripple` now run every unit test.
- **Two analysis bugs found by editing editor files by hand, now fixed with regression tests:** `this` inside static methods was not followed, so changing `MoveCaretCommand.getEditOperations` selected no test (the cursor reaches it through `CommandExecutor`'s `this._innerExecuteCommands(...)` chain). A static and an instance member with the same name shared a key, so a comment in `Position.isBefore` selected 819 test files. On 630 commits of `main`, the first fix adds 19 test files to one commit and the second removes spurious selections from nine. Re-scoring the saved CI failures: nothing that was selected before is missed now.
- **Five more false negatives from review, fixed with regression tests:** repository paths named from the root in strings (the syntax highlighting fixture reads its grammars as `'extensions/.../*.tmLanguage.json'`), reordered object members with load-time effects, constructors with side effects (`new X()`), mutations of module state other than `x = ...` (`push`, `set`, property writes, including through called functions), and static setters hidden behind their getter. On the same 708 commits, 206 select more tests, none newly exceed the 50% limit, and the mean stays 9.0%. Re-scoring the saved CI failures misses nothing that was selected before.
- **Three more from the second review round:** snapshot-only changes now select the tests that read that `__snapshots__` folder (found from the folder name in their code, which also caught `test-cases` fixtures that nothing selected), `build/package*.json` (the transpiler's packages, such as esbuild) runs every unit test, and packages loaded through `importAMDNodeModule` are tracked (`moduleLoaders`). On the same 708 commits, the mean stays 9.0% and nothing previously selected is missed.
- **Every test data location probed:** editing one data file in each of the 52 folders of non-module files under `src/**/test` found one more gap: the keyboard mapper's golden files and layouts, which `keyboardMapperTestUtils.ts` reads through template literals, selected no test. A template literal whose static start names a folder now reads the data files there that match its static start and end, so `win_de_ch.txt` selects both keyboard mapper tests while `` `./file${i}.ts` `` reads nothing. On the same 708 commits the plans are unchanged, and re-scoring the saved CI failures misses nothing that was selected before.
- **Six more from the third review round, fixed with regression tests:** a failed plan download (such as a digest mismatch, which download-artifact reports after extracting) now discards the partial plan, so macOS and Windows run every unit test instead of trusting it. Adding or reordering npm package imports (`import 'polyfill';`) selects the tests that load the module, since packages are not analyzed. Object literal properties that a later spread or computed key can overwrite (`{ a: 1, ...overrides }`) depend on the whole object. A version change of a package that a `runEverything` script loads (`yaserver` serves the browser tests) runs every unit test: ripple finds these packages itself, which replaces the hand-written toolchain list. An `allowScripts` change reaches the packages that depend on the package (`bufferutil` → `ws`). On the same 708 commits the plans are unchanged; of the 220 commits since July that change `package.json` or `package-lock.json`, 42 instead of 41 run every unit test.
- **Nine more from the fourth review round, fixed with regression tests:** the evaluation order of load-time effects is now compared as a whole (loading a module directly that a later import loaded before, swapping a module and a package import, and package subpaths selected nothing); dynamic imports and namespace imports of barrels reach what the re-exports bind to; a module that does not parse runs every unit test; changes that reach what the test runners call (`assertCleanState`, the Electron protocol handlers) run every unit test; `remote/.npmrc`, `build/.npmrc`, `build/.cachesalt` and the `node_modules` cache key helpers run every unit test; pull requests that change `build/ripple` and break its build, tests or planning get a failed check (other pull requests only get a warning); and full hygiene skips `build/ripple/target`. On the same 708 commits the mean stays 9.0%: 11 commits select more tests, 16 fewer, and none newly run everything. Re-scoring the saved CI failures misses nothing that was selected before.
- **Two more from a parallel review:** methods that code outside the analysis calls by name were never reached (Node.js streams call `_flush` and `_write`, the DOM calls `connectedCallback`, xterm calls an addon's `activate`), so changing them skipped the class's own tests. A class that extends or implements a global, a Node.js module or an npm package, directly or through its analyzed superclasses, now has all of its methods reached with it (2,223 methods of 687 classes). Changing `build/lib/electronVersion.ts` planned no tests: ripple now follows the relative imports of the `runEverything` scripts (35 more build scripts, changed by 12 of 5,636 commits in 90 days). On the same 708 commits the mean stays 9.0% (one commit selects one more test file), and re-scoring the saved CI failures misses nothing that was selected before.
- **Two more reviews:** a load-time read of module state moved across load-time code that changes the state (`const snapshot = state.items.length` before `state.items.push(1)`), local functions passed to load-time calls (`[1].map(write)`), `Object` methods that change their argument (`Object.defineProperties`, `Object.freeze`), writes of a whole object read through its members (`config.mode`), cycles of re-exports (each whole-module reference now depends on one node per module, so cycles are cycles of the graph) and package interfaces implemented through analyzed re-exports or interfaces are covered, with regression tests. `gulpfile.mjs` and the Windows install helper `exec.ps1` run every unit test. Moving a method still changes nothing: methods are not enumerable, no test depends on their order, and counting it would make 44 of 708 commits select more tests. On the same 708 commits the plans are unchanged, and re-scoring the saved CI failures misses nothing that was selected before.

Commands run locally (macOS), with results:

- `cd build/ripple && cargo test --release --locked`: 68 passed
- `cd build/ripple && cargo build --release --locked`: passed, no warnings
- `ripple plan --config build/ripple/vscode.jsonc --base 2a70c61feb^ --head 2a70c61feb --out-dir .build/unit-test-plan` (#342623): 835 unit test files, 38.8% of the unit test work
- `npm run test-node -- --runList .build/unit-test-plan/unit.txt`: ran 64 of the 835 files, 1,885 passing, 0 failing
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --browser chromium --runList .build/unit-test-plan/unit.txt`: ran 770 of the 835 files, 20,628 passing, 1 failing (`Chat Pet Colors`, a 5 s timeout under load; it passes when run alone: `--run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatPetColors.test.ts`, 27 passing)
- `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 ./scripts/test.sh --runList .build/unit-test-plan/unit.txt`: ran 831 of the 835 files (4 were newer than the local build), 22,351 passing, 0 failing
- A browser run whose list has no browser tests exits with 0 without launching a browser
- `cd build && npm run typecheck`: passed
- `npm run eslint -- test/unit/node/index.js test/unit/browser/index.js test/unit/electron/index.js test/unit/electron/renderer.js`: passed
- `node build/hygiene.ts <changed files>`: passed

**On GitHub Actions:** a temporary commit (reverted) planned #342662 instead of this PR, so this PR's own run went through the selection path ([run](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39519293573)):

| Job | Today (mean) | Validation run | Ran |
|---|---|---|---|
| macOS (run) / Electron-Unit | 14.4 min | 2 min 37 s | 20 Electron files (4,029 tests), 8 node.js files (2,364 tests) |
| Windows (run) / Electron-Unit | 19.9 min | 3 min 58 s | 20 Electron files (4,032 tests), 8 node.js files (2,367 tests) |
| macOS (unit) / Browser | 8.4 min | 1 min 57 s | 12 files (1,666 tests, WebKit) |
| Windows (unit) / Browser | 10.4 min | 2 min 36 s | 12 files (1,666 tests, Chromium) |

All four jobs downloaded the plan's single `unit.txt`, and each runner picked its own files from it (20 Electron, 8 node.js, 12 browser: the same files as the earlier per-runner lists). Without a plan, the jobs download nothing, report no error and run every unit test (for example 45,139 browser tests on Windows in [this run](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39517617318)). With a warm cache, planning takes about 25 s; a cold build of ripple, including its tests, takes under a minute.

## Notes for reviewers

- This PR's own run selects every unit test because it changes the test runners. The savings show on PRs after this one merges.
- The core test jobs already wait for `Detect Changes` (#342729). With a warm cache, planning adds about 10 to 15 s to it: a full depth-2 checkout (9 s) instead of a sparse one, and about 5 s to plan.
- `build/ripple` also contains the analysis commands behind the numbers above (`replay`, `blame`); CI only uses `plan`.
- oxc needs Rust 1.97 or newer; `rust-toolchain.toml` pins 1.99.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The diff directly removes sparse checkout, Git sparse checkout affects worktree population rather than availability of already-fetched commit objects, ripple reads repository content by object ID through `git ls-tree` and `git cat-file`, and the only worktree paths used here are the two local actions plus `build/ripple`. All downstream jobs explicitly depend on `changes`, so this I/O is on their critical path.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem writes, worktree bytes, and checkout CPU
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The extra work is proportional to the number and size of files in the repository and occurs once on every PR workflow run, before all `needs: changes` jobs can start.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased latency and excessive filesystem I/O on the CI critical path
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The Detect Changes checkout materialized only `.github/actions/detect-changes` and `.github/actions/detect-agent-host-e2e-changes`; repository blobs for the fetched commit were still available through Git object commands.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: `actions/checkout` now populates the full VS Code working tree before change detection instead of materializing only the two local action directories. The additional depth is required, but removing sparse checkout is not required for `git ls-tree`/`git cat-file` access.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The hunk deletes the existing `sparse-checkout` list and replaces it with the added claim at RIGHT line 57 that the checkout cannot remain sparse, leaving only `fetch-depth: 2`; this changes the worktree from two action directories to the entire repository on every PR run.
Findings.Title: Keep the Detect Changes working tree sparse
Findings.Impact: Every pull-request push performs unnecessary full-repository worktree materialization and delays all jobs gated on Detect Changes; the added filesystem I/O grows with repository size even when the PR ultimately needs no unit tests.
Findings.Evidence: `Engine::snapshot` calls `git ls-tree` and `BlobReader` runs `git cat-file --batch`, so ripple reads blobs from the Git object database, not from checked-out files. `fetch-depth: 2` can therefore be combined with sparse checkout. The workflow itself only executes `./.github/actions/detect-changes`, `./.github/actions/detect-agent-host-e2e-changes`, and files under `build/ripple`; meanwhile 29 jobs declare `needs: changes`, making the unnecessary worktree expansion gate broad CI progress.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep `fetch-depth: 2`, restore sparse checkout, and add `build/ripple` to the existing two action paths. This leaves both commits' objects available to `ls-tree`/`cat-file` while avoiding a full worktree checkout.

Scenarios.Scenario: Every pull-request push runs Detect Changes and computes the unit-test plan before the dependent CI matrix starts.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Checkout, both existing change-detection actions, ripple cache restore/build, `ripple plan`, and conditional plan upload all execute in the `changes` job. The 29 jobs declaring `needs: changes` cannot progress until it completes, so the newly expanded checkout and planning work are on the broad CI critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch two commits and populate the full repository worktree with `actions/checkout`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per PR workflow run; worktree writes scale with every tracked repository file rather than the three directories needed by the job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Checkout populated only the two local action directories via sparse checkout. Fetching another commit is new and required, but full worktree materialization is not.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks Detect Changes and therefore all `needs: changes` jobs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore the source-hashed ripple binary cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cache request per PR run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No ripple cache access or planner existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must resolve before planning; a hit avoids compilation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: On a cache miss, install Rust and run release `cargo test` and `cargo build`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per cache miss; dependency/toolchain downloads and compilation cover the complete new Rust crate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Rust toolchain installation or Cargo build ran in Detect Changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds up to the configured ten-minute build step before planning; unrelated PRs normally use the main-branch cache, while ripple-changing PRs intentionally miss on a new source hash.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate two Git trees, read module blobs through batched `git cat-file` workers, and diff the commits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two `ls-tree` calls, about four `cat-file` processes per Rayon thread for the base analysis plus bounded workers for changed head blobs, one long-lived selection blob reader, and one `diff-tree`; unchanged head blobs hit the in-process OID cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Detect Changes did not enumerate, parse, or graph repository modules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Supplies all analyzer input and must finish before a plan exists.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build two declaration graphs and serialize `plan.json` plus an optional `unit.txt`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two whole-repository graph builds per run; analysis facts are shared for equal blob IDs. Output contains each selected unit-test path once after HashSet deduplication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No impact graph or unit-test plan was generated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: CPU, allocation, and output writes are synchronous in `ripple plan`.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Upload the selected unit-test plan artifact.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one artifact per PR run, only when selective execution applies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The changes job waits for upload completion; consumers need the artifact after this job.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call GitHub APIs from the two existing change-detection composite actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One invocation of each action per PR run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same two actions ran after the sparse checkout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing serialized work in Detect Changes remains on the critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Repository worktree size, all configured TypeScript modules and declaration/edge counts, plus changed module blobs. Current design deduplicates unchanged base/head analysis by OID, but still builds both complete graphs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Workflow steps are serialized. Ripple parses modules on Rayon’s global pool; `Engine::fill` creates roughly four chunks per Rayon thread for the base snapshot and runs at most the pool width concurrently, each chunk with its own `git cat-file --batch` process. The head snapshot reuses OID-keyed analysis facts and only analyzes changed/new blobs, while both graphs are linked serially.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The ripple executable has an exact source/toolchain cache key. A warm hit skips Cargo entirely; a miss builds and saves. Parsed `FileFacts` are cached only in-process by blob OID, so unchanged base/head modules are parsed once per run but every workflow run rebuilds the analysis cache. Missing/failed planning produces no trusted artifact and deliberately falls back to full tests.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the checkout hunk, `needs: changes` fan-out, Git object-based reader, OID cache, Rayon scheduling, and graph construction are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact checkout bytes and seconds vary with runner filesystem and repository growth; the full-worktree versus three-directory cardinality and its placement before every dependent job are certain. Ripple’s own analysis duration also varies with runner cores and change size.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity eager I/O regression: removing sparse checkout materializes the entire worktree even though ripple reads all other content from fetched Git objects. The analyzer’s bounded parallelism, OID reuse, and two-graph work otherwise have evidence of deliberate bounded behavior rather than a separate high-confidence regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: macOS and Windows Electron, Node, and browser unit-test jobs consume the plan and run only selected files.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each of four unit-test jobs downloads the artifact before its test steps. Within a job the Electron, Node, and browser steps remain serial workflow steps; each runner first discovers its default test files, intersects them with the plan, and then starts only its supported selected tests. When `plan.json` exists without `unit.txt`, the test steps are skipped; when no trusted plan exists, the prior full-suite path runs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One download attempt in each selected macOS/Windows unit job, four total in the full unit matrix; one artifact contains the shared deduplicated list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Jobs did not download a test plan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes test execution in each job. Failed downloads delete partial output and fall back to full tests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read `unit.txt`, glob the runner’s normal test files, and filter by Set membership.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One list read and one existing full candidate-file discovery per runner invocation; selected effective cardinality is the intersection of the shared list with that runner’s test family.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Runners discovered and loaded every default test file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous setup before launching/running tests; filtering prevents unselected modules from loading.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Reusable macOS/Windows workflows and test/unit runners
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch Electron, Node, and browser test processes for the selected files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same runner-step cardinality as before when the shared list is nonempty; test-module work is bounded to selected files, with browser exiting before launch when its intersection is empty.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same runners launched and executed their entire supported suites.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dominates each unit job after selection.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of selected unique test files after declaration-graph deduplication, capped by the 50% weighted-work fallback. Each runner filters that set against its existing candidate glob.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The four macOS/Windows unit jobs can run in parallel. Artifact download occurs once per job. Selection is a Set membership filter; no per-selected-file network or IPC fan-out is added. Individual runner process/browser behavior remains controlled by the pre-existing runners.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The artifact is per workflow run, with no cross-run cache. Presence of `plan.json` selects plan mode; absence or failed download is a negative state that safely runs all tests. An empty valid selection has `plan.json` but no `unit.txt`, causing the unit steps to skip. Runner file discovery is not newly cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: artifact conditions, fallback states, Set construction, candidate filtering, and browser zero-match exit are explicit in changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runner startup overhead for a shared list containing no tests of one family varies, especially Electron, but it replaces a full-suite run rather than adding work relative to the pre-diff scenario.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable regression. The new artifact/read overhead is bounded and enables a much larger reduction in test execution; failure and empty-selection paths are coalesced into full-run or skip behavior rather than per-file boundary calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: The main-branch Ripple workflow maintains the executable cache after source changes and on a daily schedule.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: This workflow is off the pull-request job critical path, but its successful cache population determines whether later PR Detect Changes runs use a warm binary or compile from source.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per push changing ripple, daily schedule, or manual dispatch; only the ripple directory is materialized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes cache lookup in this maintenance workflow and is off the active PR critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Lookup the exact ripple binary cache without downloading it on hit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A hit ends the expensive path; a miss triggers the build.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install pinned Rust, run release tests, build release binary, and save it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per cache miss; save is one binary artifact under the exact source hash.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Determines cache availability for future PRs but does not block an already-running PR.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Ripple source/dependency compilation size and frequency of source changes or cache eviction, not repository test count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A workflow-level concurrency group serializes runs for the same workflow/ref and does not cancel an in-progress build. Steps are serial; Cargo provides its own compile parallelism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Exact positive cache entries are keyed by OS plus Cargo manifests, toolchain, and all Rust sources. Lookup-only avoids binary transfer on a hit. A miss performs and saves one build; the daily run repairs eviction. There is no negative cache, so persistent build failures retry daily, which is bounded by schedule and timeout.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: triggers, exact key, lookup-only behavior, build condition, save condition, and concurrency group are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold Cargo duration and cache eviction frequency vary, but execution is daily/change-triggered and timeout-bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The bounded maintenance cost is intentionally off the PR critical path and prevents repeated cold builds across unrelated pull requests.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 26 changed files and all diff pages. Submitted one medium-severity finding for unnecessary full-worktree checkout on the broad Detect Changes critical path. Traced planner analysis/cache/concurrency, artifact fan-out, runner filtering/fallbacks, and cache-maintenance workflows; no other diff-caused performance regression met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
